rationale: A private type alias in the readability extractor that maps HTML nodes to scoring candidates. It is an internal implementation detail of the content-extraction algorithm with no behaviour of its own, not an architectural element.

Trivial config accessor returning the negation of a parsed boolean option (DISABLE_HTTP_SERVICE). It is an implementation detail of the configuration options component, below the granularity of an architecture element, and it implements no cross-cutting concern itself.

A private Go interface combining io.WriteCloser with Reset, used internally by the response builder for compression writers. It is an implementation detail with no architectural identity, no callers listed, and no cross-cutting concern of its own.

Client-side keyboard shortcut dispatcher (Miniflux-style UI) that binds key sequences to callbacks on document keydown. It is a reusable user-input interaction mechanism used across views, so it is best modelled as a UX action pattern (keyboard modality triggering actions). It is notable but not core architecture.

A single unit test function verifying that config validation accepts the OIDC provider when a discovery endpoint is set. It is a test case, modelled at most as a test case sketch, and has minor significance. It only parses config strings, so it implements no cross-cutting concern itself.

A trivial slice type alias over MediaCategory used while parsing media RSS feeds. It has no behaviour, callers or callees, and sits well below the granularity a maintainer would name as an architectural element.

A Go generic type constraint (int | int64 | float64) with no callers. It is a language-level type-parameter helper, not a domain schema or architectural element. It is an implementation detail below modelling granularity.

A Go unit test that verifies concurrent lazy population of the locale translation catalog under the race detector. It is a single test case for an internal helper, so it maps to a testing test case sketch of minor significance. It implements none of the cross-cutting concerns itself.

Storage-layer method issuing a single UPDATE against the feeds table, keyed by feed id and user_id. This is an application-issued write query against one collection, so it is a data-store access pattern. It is notable and used by the API, UI and Google Reader handlers, but it remains a single query rather than a store.

This is the main front-end JavaScript module of the Miniflux web UI. It bootstraps the client-side behaviour: click and keyboard handlers, forms, the menu, the media player, the service worker and WebAuthn wiring. As the app-wide client root it is a core UX element. The WebAuthn work is delegated to an initializer, so authentication is not marked here.

Client-side WebAuthn handler implementing passkey registration and login ceremonies against server endpoints. It is the browser-side authentication mechanism: it verifies identity via credentials. It is best modelled as part of the security layer's authentication configuration (WebAuthn mechanism). It also renders error alerts in the DOM and calls the browser credential API and backend HTTP endpoints.

A private one-method interface abstracting sql.Row/sql.Rows Scan, used to share row-scanning code for web sessions inside the storage package. It is an implementation helper below the granularity of an architectural element and does no persistence work itself.

A small private helper that writes a preferences cookie holding language and theme after logout. It is a UI-support detail, not authentication logic, and sits below architectural granularity. It is minor and file-local. It touches the user interface only by persisting display preferences in the client.

Method on the Karakeep integration client that POSTs an entry URL to the third-party Karakeep API with a bearer token, then attaches tags. It is the core behaviour of an external integration adapter, invoked internally by SendEntry. Supplying a configured API token is not identity verification, so authentication is false.

Client-side JS module implementing swipe gestures (swipe to toggle entry status, swipe to page) in the web UI. It is a reusable touch-input interaction recipe with visual feedback that is applied across entry items and content, so it fits a UX ActionPattern. It is a notable but not core UI element.

An unexported slice type alias over opmlOutline, used only for OPML serialization inside the opml package. It is a trivial implementation detail with no behaviour and no published schema of its own, so it falls below the granularity of an architecture element.

Central abstraction for OAuth2 identity providers (e.g. Google, OIDC): it supplies the OAuth2 config, exchanges authorization codes for tokens and links external identities to users. This is the authentication mechanism contract, so it is a security-layer AuthenticationConfig, and it integrates with external identity providers.

A single Go unit test verifying that the Atom 1.0 parser leaves Language empty when the feed has none. It is one test case among many in the parser's suite, so it maps to a testcasesketch of minor significance. It implements no cross-cutting concerns.

Trivial fluent builder setter that only flips a boolean flag on the feed query builder. It performs no storage access itself and is an implementation detail of the query-building component, not an architectural element.

Client-side WebAuthn module that drives passkey registration and login against the server endpoints, using the browser credentials API. Identity-verification logic is security-layer evidence for the WebAuthn authentication mechanism. It also renders error alerts in the UI and calls server HTTP endpoints.

HTTP route handler for the DELETE user endpoint in Miniflux's REST API, so it is an API operation contract. It performs an admin check and blocks self-removal itself (authorization). Persistence is delegated to store calls, so data_persistence is not marked. It is a significant endpoint.

A trivial slice type alias of InlineKeyboardButton pointers inside the Telegram bot client package. It is a minor payload helper type for the external API request shape, below the granularity a maintainer would name, so it is not modelled as an architectural element.

Trivial constructor that initializes a Builder struct with defaults. Although widely called, it is boilerplate. The Builder type or response package might be modelled as an application component, but this factory function is an implementation detail below architectural granularity.

A single Go unit test checking that icon URL discovery returns no results for HTML without icon links. It is a test-layer artifact realizing one test case (no-icons outcome). It is a minor element, relevant only to the icon finder test file.

A browser service worker script, deployed as a unit, that pre-caches an offline page at install and serves it for navigation requests when the network is unavailable. It is a self-contained client-side component providing offline-fallback behaviour. It persists content in Cache Storage. It is not a view, a route or an API contract.

This private method of the Wallabag integration client obtains an OAuth2 password-grant access token by calling Wallabag's /oauth/v2/token endpoint. It authenticates against an external third-party API. It is an internal helper used only by CreateEntry, so it is a minor application function rather than a standalone architectural element.

An exported slice type in the domain model package that defines an ordered list of Enclosure entities, used for entry attachments. It is a list-valued data shape, so arrayschema fits. Its significance is minor: it is a thin collection alias over the Enclosure entity and adds no constraints of its own.

A trivial slice type alias over Category used as a list container. It carries no fields, behaviour or schema of its own beyond the Category entity, so it falls below modelling granularity; the Category entity itself would be the data-model element.

A repository method issuing an ad hoc SQL write against the entries table: it deletes aged entries and inserts tombstones. This is a named write operation sent from application code to the store, so it is an access pattern. It is notable within the storage module, but it is not a core boundary.

A string type alias used as an enum of mark-as-read behaviors inside the settings form. It is a small form-local type with no behavior or published schema, used only by NewSettingsForm. That makes it an implementation detail rather than a named architectural element.

A single Go unit test checking that the RDF parser defaults a missing item date to the current time. It is a test case realizing one coverage scenario for the RDF parser. It is a minor unit, and it implements no cross-cutting concerns itself.

A table-driven Go unit test that checks how the feed entry regex filter (matchesEntryRegexRules) handles invalid regex patterns. It is a single test case design with concrete inputs and expected outcomes, so it maps to testcasesketch. It is minor in architectural significance and implements no cross-cutting concerns.

A trivial int type alias used as a key type for storing values in Go request contexts. It is boilerplate plumbing with no behaviour or architectural role, below the granularity of any modelled element.

Parses user-level and feed-level filter rule text into a rule list for the feed entry filter. It is used by the feed processor and is a small internal parsing step inside the filter module. It is minor application behaviour with no cross-cutting concerns.

HTTP route handler in Miniflux's web UI that triggers a feed refresh for the current user and then redirects to the feed entries page. It is one method-path endpoint contract, so it is modelled as an API operation. It logs failures via slog and drives the UI with an HTML redirect; the refresh logic itself is delegated.

HTTP handler implementing the Fever API 'mark feed as read' operation, dispatched from serve. It parses form inputs, delegates persistence to the store, and returns a JSON response. It is one operation of an external-client-compatible API contract. The debug log line is incidental rather than telemetry design.

An int type alias that enumerates tokenizer states inside the srcset parser of the HTML sanitizer. It is a private implementation detail of parsing logic, not an architectural element, and implements none of the cross-cutting concerns.

An individual Go unit test verifying that the RSS parser normalizes the channel language. It is a single test case in a large parser test file. It belongs to the testing layer as a test case sketch and has minor architectural significance. It implements no cross-cutting concern.

A private storage method that syncs an entry's enclosures by issuing SQL inserts and deletes against the enclosures table within a transaction. It is a write access pattern on one collection, but it is an internal helper called only by updateEntry, so its significance is minor.

A single Go unit test checking that the locale printer's Printf falls back to formatting the raw format string when the translation key is missing. It is an individual test case of minor significance, scoped to the locale package, and implements no cross-cutting concern itself.

A bare integer type alias used to enumerate kinds of rewrite-rule validation errors. It is an implementation detail inside the content-rewrite validation code, with no behaviour, callers or architectural role of its own, so it would not be recorded as a model element.

A trivial slice type alias over imageCandidate, used only by the srcset sanitizer helper. It is an internal implementation detail of HTML sanitization, below the granularity at which an architecture model would record an element.

A table-driven unit test that exercises the proxy URL validation of feed modification requests with empty, valid and invalid partitions. It is a testing artifact best modelled as a test case sketch. It is minor and local to the validator module.

An interface method declaration that only returns the provider's OAuth2 configuration. It is an accessor on the Provider abstraction, not an element in its own right. The Provider interface is the authentication-relevant element; this method performs no identity verification itself and has no callers or callees.

A private helper on the Shaarli integration client that builds an HMAC-signed JWT bearer token from the API secret, so it implements outbound authentication credential generation. It is a minor internal unit, but its substance is authentication to the external Shaarli API, which places it in the security layer.

A trivial slice type alias over Job with no behaviour, no callers and no published schema of its own. It is a convenience collection type below modelling granularity; the Job entity itself would be the modelled element.

Small DOM helper in Miniflux front-end JS that adjusts unread counter spans and the page title by a delta. It is a UI implementation detail called only by updateEntriesStatus, below the granularity of a modelled UX element, though it does drive the user interface.

Trivial accessor returning a stored OAuth2 state field. Although the state supports CSRF protection in the OAuth flow, this getter performs no verification itself. It is an implementation detail of the Authorization type, not an architectural element.

A private Go int type alias used as an enum discriminator for config option value types. It is an implementation detail with no callers or behaviour, so it sits below the granularity of an architecture element.

Trivial constructor that only builds a csrfMiddleware struct holding a base path. The CSRF protection itself (a security countermeasure) lives in the middleware type and its methods, not in this factory. It is boilerplate below the modelling granularity.

A repository-layer method that issues a single named UPDATE against the entries collection, keyed by user and status and joined to feeds and categories. It is an application-issued write query, so it is a data-store access pattern of moderate significance. The debug log line is incidental, not telemetry design.

A trivial slice type alias over APIKey with no behaviour, callers or callees. It is boilerplate collection typing below the granularity a maintainer would name; the APIKey entity itself would be the modelled element, not this collection alias.

A single Go unit test verifying that user-modification validation rejects password changes when local auth is disabled. It is a test case exercising validation logic, so it maps to testing/testcasesketch with low significance. It configures and asserts rather than implementing auth itself, so no concerns apply.

A trivial slice alias of User used to hold a collection. It adds no shape or behaviour beyond the User entity itself, so it falls below the granularity of an architecture element. The User object schema is what would be modelled.

The Apprise integration client's method that POSTs entry notifications to an external Apprise /notify endpoint. It is the behaviour of an integration adapter, invoked internally by PushEntries, so it is an application function rather than an exposed service. Its debug logging is incidental rather than telemetry design.

A single Go unit test verifying that ValidateUserModification accepts empty filter rules. It is a test case in the testing layer, mapping to a test case sketch. It is narrow and of minor significance, and it implements none of the cross-cutting concerns itself.

Trivial config accessor returning a parsed option string (POLLING_SCHEDULER). It is a getter on the configuration options struct with no logic of its own, so it sits below the granularity of an architecture element.

A private type alias mapping locale keys to translation dictionaries inside an internal locale package. It has no behaviour, no callers or callees, and sits below the level a maintainer would name as an architectural element. It is only an implementation detail of localisation.

A single unit test function that checks the OPML parser's handling of unescaped ampersands. It is one concrete test case, best modelled as a test case sketch for the OPML parse coverage target. It has minor significance and implements none of the cross-cutting concerns.

An individual unit test function checking that the JSON feed parser trims trailing whitespace from the site URL. It belongs to the testing layer as a single test case realizing a sketch. It is minor, one of many parser edge-case tests, and implements no cross-cutting concerns.

A slice type alias with custom unmarshalling, used to tolerate malformed JSON Feed 'authors' fields. It is a parsing detail inside the JSON feed reader. It is below the granularity of an architectural element, though slightly notable within its own file.

Internal method of the icon finder that fetches a website's HTML page over HTTP, extracts icon URLs and downloads the first usable icon. It is a step within feed icon discovery, internal to the iconFinder component. It makes outbound HTTP requests, so external_integration is true. Its debug logging is incidental, so observability is false.

Server-side HTTP handler for the POST that renames a WebAuthn credential. It enforces an ownership check (forbidden if the credential belongs to another user), validates the form, updates the name in storage, re-renders the HTML form on error and redirects on success. It is best modelled as one route operation of modest significance.

DescriptionList is a trivial slice type alias over Description, used to parse media:description elements in RSS/Media feeds. It is a parsing implementation detail with no behaviour or callers, so it falls below the granularity of an architecture element.

A single unit test checking how one config option (OAUTH2_REDIRECT_URL) is parsed, covering its default and a set value. It is a minor test case, modelled as a test case sketch. It exercises config parsing only and implements no auth logic itself.

A trivial slice type alias over Feed with no behaviour, no callers, and no fields of its own. It is a collection convenience below the granularity a maintainer would name. The Feed entity itself would be modelled as the object schema, not this alias.

A small private factory that builds an http.Server with configured timeouts. It is an implementation detail of StartWebServer, not an element a maintainer would name on its own. The web server component itself would be modelled instead.

Trivial mutator on WebSession that nils out pending OAuth2 flow state and marks the session dirty. Although it relates to an OAuth2 login flow, it does no verification itself. It is an accessor-level implementation detail below modelling granularity.

Trivial accessor on ProxyRotator that returns whether the proxy list is non-empty. It has no logic beyond a length check and is an implementation detail below the granularity of an architecture element.

A trivial slice type alias over subscription pointers used in feed discovery. It carries no behaviour or schema of its own and sits below the granularity a maintainer would name as an architectural element.

Small helper method on the atomLinks slice that selects the alternate/HTML link from an Atom feed during parsing. It is an implementation detail of the Atom reader, below the granularity of an architecture element, and implements no cross-cutting concern.

A Go unit test that checks the plain-text HTTP response helper returns the expected status code, body and content type. It is a single test case against a minor utility, so it maps to a testing test case sketch of low significance. The callee list reflects name-resolution noise; the test exercises no cross-cutting concern.

A private Go function type alias used internally by the media proxy rewriter. It is an implementation detail with no behaviour of its own, below the granularity at which the architecture model records elements.

An unexported int type alias used as an internal enum for the HTTP server's listener mode. It has no behaviour, callers or callees, and sits below the granularity a maintainer would name in an architecture model, so it is an implementation detail.

This is a table-driven Go unit test of GitHub feed URL discovery in the subscription finder. As a test asset it belongs to the testing layer as a test case realizing coverage of one function. Its significance is minor, and it implements no cross-cutting concern itself: no network calls are made and the URLs are only parsed.

A private one-line wrapper around http.Request.PathValue, used only by two sibling param helpers. It is a trivial implementation detail with no architectural identity, so it is not a model element and implements no cross-cutting concern.

Trivial config accessor returning the parsed OAUTH2_PROVIDER option string. Although its value drives OAuth2 setup elsewhere, the getter itself performs no authentication and is an implementation detail below modelling granularity.

A Stringer method that formats config options as key=value lines. This is a trivial formatting helper. The caller count likely reflects name-resolution noise across many String methods. It is not an architectural element on its own.

A single Go unit test verifying that LocalizedErrorWrapper translates a message key with no arguments. It belongs in the testing layer as an individual test case. Its significance is minimal: one narrow test case in a locale package. It implements none of the cross-cutting concerns.

Miniflux's background metrics collector loop periodically queries storage counts and DB pool stats, then sets Prometheus gauges. It is telemetry instrumentation code, a manual instrumentation site for the metric instruments. The daemon starts it. It reads the database through store queries and emits metrics plus logs.

A private slice type alias over AtomPerson used in Atom feed parsing. It is a trivial collection helper type with no behaviour or independent architectural meaning, below the granularity a maintainer would name when explaining the system.

KeyboardHandler is a reusable client-side module that registers keyboard shortcut combinations, listens to document keydown events and dispatches callbacks. It drives the UI, but it renders no view and is not a single UI control, so it fits best as a front-end application component. A maintainer would name it when explaining shortcut handling.

Small encoding utility that wraps a byte buffer in a UTF-8 charset-converting reader. It is a text-decoding helper inside the feed reader package, below the granularity a maintainer would name as an architectural element. It does no I/O to external systems or storage itself.

A trivial predicate on the OPML outline data structure that checks whether FeedURL is non-empty. It is an accessor-level helper used during OPML parsing and marshalling, an implementation detail rather than an architectural element.

A trivial slice type alias over Icon with no callers and no behaviour. It is a collection convenience type rather than a named architectural element. The Icon type itself would be the modelled data object.

Shared HTTP response helper that logs a warning and writes a 401 JSON error. It is a reusable utility for response formatting, not an architectural element on its own; callers perform the authentication. It does emit structured logs, so observability applies.

Trivial accessor returning a parsed boolean config option (HTTPS flag) from the options map. It is a getter with no logic. Callers use it for cookie and middleware decisions, but the method itself implements no concern and sits below modelling granularity.

Miniflux front-end touch gesture handler: swipe on entries toggles read status, swipe on content navigates pages. It is a reusable interaction recipe (swipe trigger plus visual feedback) applied across entry items, so it fits a UX action pattern. It is a notable UI behaviour unit, not a core architectural element.

A trivial setter on the WebSession model that assigns the language and theme fields without marking the session dirty. It is an accessor-level implementation detail with no behaviour or I/O of its own, so it is not an architectural element.

Trivial private helper that formats an error, logs it via slog, prints to stderr and exits. It is an implementation detail of server startup, not an architectural element. It does emit a log record and CLI output, so observability and user_interface are marked true.

A private integer type alias used as an enum discriminator for where a proxy setting comes from inside the request builder. It is a trivial implementation detail with no behaviour, callers or architectural identity of its own.

A unit test function checking that one config option (METRICS_PASSWORD) defaults to empty and parses correctly. It is a single test case in the testing layer with minor significance. It only parses configuration lines and does not itself authenticate anyone or emit telemetry.

A small Storage method that issues a single query to read the PostgreSQL server version, used only by the about page. It touches the database directly, but it is a minor diagnostic query rather than a domain access pattern, so its significance is low.

A trivial slice type alias over Entry with no fields or behaviour of its own. The Entry entity is the meaningful data-model element. This collection alias is an implementation convenience used by UI handlers, so it falls below modelling granularity.

A trivial private helper that formats an icon URL path from the base path and a static bundle checksum. It is used only by showWebManifest and sits at the implementation-detail level, so it would not be modelled as an architectural element.

Trivial constructor returning an empty archive.org Client struct. The Client itself is the integration component, but this zero-complexity factory is boilerplate below modelling granularity and performs no external calls itself.

A small unit test function verifying IsValidRegex with a table of two inputs. It is a test case in the testing layer, realizing a test case sketch. It is minor and local to the validator package, and it implements none of the cross-cutting concerns.

A private slice type alias over AtomLink pointers, used in Atom feed parsing to hang helper methods. It is an implementation detail of the feed parser with no callers recorded and no architectural meaning of its own, below the granularity of a model element.

An unexported slice type alias over filterRule, used internally by the reader filter package. It has no behaviour or published shape of its own and sits below architectural granularity, so it is an implementation detail.

An HTTP route handler in the REST API that creates a feed (likely POST /v1/feeds). It decodes the request, defaults the category, validates, delegates creation, and returns a 201 JSON response. It is an API operation contract and a significant external integration point. Persistence goes through store and reader calls rather than being done here.

Constructor that configures the OAuth2 authentication mechanism, selecting and registering an OIDC or Google identity provider with client credentials. It is evidence for the authentication configuration. It integrates with external IdPs, since OIDC discovery calls the endpoint. Its logging is incidental, and as a factory it ranks as a notable but not central unit.

Miniflux Omnivore integration client method that sends a GraphQL mutation to the external Omnivore API to save a URL. It is the core behaviour of this integration adapter and is invoked by SendEntry. It attaches an API token header but does not verify identity itself, so only external_integration applies.

A bare integer type alias used as an enum discriminator for Google Reader stream kinds. On its own it is an implementation detail of the Google Reader compatibility API, below the granularity of an architectural element. Its only caller is a test.

A trivial accessor-style helper on the Enclosure data model that checks whether the MIME type has a video/ prefix. It is an implementation detail of the entity, not an architectural element in its own right, and it implements none of the cross-cutting concerns.

A private slice type alias over atomCategory used inside the Atom feed parser. It is a trivial data-holding helper with no behaviour of its own and sits below the granularity of an architecture element.

A single unit test function verifying that NewCharsetReader decodes KOI8-R content to UTF-8 from a content-type charset. It is an individual test case realizing a test case sketch, and its significance is minor and local to the encoding package's test file.

Private helper in the HTML sanitizer that checks a URL against a blocklist of substrings (e.g., tracking pixels). It is a trivial string-matching implementation detail below modelling granularity, used only by the sanitizer's attribute functions.

A small client-side keyboard-shortcut helper that dispatches to list-item navigation or a page link. It is an implementation detail of the UI script, not a route, view or navigation transition a maintainer would model, though it does drive the user interface.

Thin middleware wrapper registering the Google Reader API-key authentication step in the handler chain. It delegates the actual credential verification to serveValidated, so it does no authentication work itself. It is the named auth entry point for the Google Reader API, giving it modest significance.

A single Go unit test function verifying that the default value and parsing of the FETCH_BILIBILI_WATCH_TIME config option work. It is a test case realization, so it belongs to the testing layer as a test case sketch. It is minor, being one of many per-option parsing tests.

Small domain-rule predicate on the Entry model that combines user settings and entry status to decide whether to auto-mark an entry as read. It is a helper method on an entity, below the granularity of an architectural element. It performs no persistence or UI rendering itself.

A small Go unit test exercising validateLanguage with one valid and one invalid locale. It is a test case in the testing layer, closest to a testcasesketch. It is a minor unit relevant only to its file and implements none of the cross-cutting concerns.

Server-rendered handler for Miniflux's Unread page. It loads the user's unread entries with pagination and renders the unread_entries template. It is a routable top-level UI screen, so it is modelled as a ux view. Persistence is delegated to the store, so data_persistence is false; rendering HTML makes user_interface true.

Custom XML unmarshaller for an inner-content helper type in the RSS parser. It only concatenates character data until the matching end element is reached. This is a low-level parsing detail rather than an architectural element. The listed callees are mis-resolved standard library calls.

An HTTP handler for the Fever API's saved_item_ids request. It is dispatched by serve, queries the store for starred entries and returns a JSON response. That makes it one operation of the Fever-compatible API contract served to external clients. The debug log is incidental, so observability is not marked.

A single Go unit test verifying config validation accepts DATABASE_MIN_CONNS equal to DATABASE_MAX_CONNS. It is a boundary-value test case within the config parsing suite, so it maps to a testing test case sketch with low significance. It touches no cross-cutting concerns directly.

Storage-layer method issuing a parameterized SELECT against the webauthn_credentials table keyed by user_id. It is a named read access pattern on one collection used by the WebAuthn UI flows. It reads credential data for authentication, but it does not verify identity itself.

A single content-rewrite rule in Miniflux's reader rewrite module that turns titled images into figure/figcaption HTML. It is a small internal transformation function, one of many rewrite rules, with only a minor role as part of the rewrite application function. It touches no I/O, auth or UI rendering.

Trivial request-context accessor that reads a timezone string with a UTC default. It is an implementation helper below the granularity of an architecture element and implements no cross-cutting concern itself.

A small formatting method on a media description struct that converts plain-text descriptions to HTML by linkifying URLs and replacing newlines with
tags. It is a trivial formatting helper, an implementation detail below architectural granularity.

A small URL utility that checks for an HTTP/HTTPS prefix and an absolute parsed URL. It is widely reused but is a helper below architectural granularity, not a service, contract or component, and it implements none of the cross-cutting concerns.

Small helper that parses the systemd WATCHDOG_USEC environment variable into a duration. It is part of the systemd watchdog integration, an infrastructure concern, but on its own it is a minor parsing utility. The listed callees look like spurious graph edges. Low significance.

A storage-layer method that issues an existing-record lookup on the feed_icons table by feed_id. This is a small read access pattern within the Storage DAO. It is minor, since it is a single existence check with one caller.

HTTP handler implementing the Fever API 'unread_item_ids' operation, dispatched from serve. It queries storage for the user's unread entry IDs and returns JSON to external Fever clients. It is one operation of a compatibility API, so it is moderately significant. The debug log is incidental and does not make it an observability element.

A thin exported wrapper that delegates to a private URL-resolution helper. It is a generic string and URL utility used by the feed parsers, and sits below the granularity of an architecture element, so it belongs to no layer.

An integration test function that exercises the GET entries API endpoint with filters (feed, pagination, ordering, search, invalid params) via the HTTP client. It is a single test case realizing coverage of an API operation, so it maps to a testing test case sketch. It is of minor significance and does no cross-cutting work itself.

Method of the Readwise integration client that POSTs an entry URL to the Readwise third-party API. It is the core behaviour of an external integration adapter, invoked internally by SendEntry. It attaches an API key header, but it does not itself verify identity. Modelled as an application function performing the external integration.

Server-side UI handler that renders the 'add_subscription' page template with categories, user and form data. It is the controller behind a specific routable screen in Miniflux's web UI, so it is best modelled as the UX view for adding a subscription. Storage reads go through store calls rather than being implemented here.

A Go unit test for the template helper 'dict', which builds a map from key/value arguments. It is a single test case against a trivial template function, so it maps to a testing test-case sketch of minor significance. It implements none of the cross-cutting concerns.
Trivial sort.Interface Len method on a private sorting helper type (byStateAndName) in the storage package. Pure boilerplate with no architectural meaning; it performs no storage I/O itself.

A private helper inside the RSS adapter. It collects enclosures from media thumbnails, enclosures, media content and peer links, resolving URLs to absolute form and removing duplicates. It is internal parsing logic called only by buildFeed. Its debug logging is incidental, so it is a minor application function rather than an architectural element in its own right.

A trivial iterator accessor on a MediaCategoryList that yields trimmed labels. It is a small helper used by the RSS parser's tag extraction and sits below the granularity a maintainer would name as an architectural element. It touches no storage, external system, UI, telemetry or security logic.

A Go benchmark that exercises the LinkTaco client's CreateBookmark against a mock HTTP server. It is a test asset that performance-tests an integration point, but it is a minor unit. It calls a mocked server rather than implementing integration itself, so no concerns apply.

Gotify client method that turns feed entries into push notifications and dispatches them through SendMessage to the external Gotify server. It is integration behaviour of the Gotify client component, invoked by PushEntries, so it is an application function. The debug log line is incidental and does not make it an observability element.

A Go benchmark function exercising the regex rule matcher for feed entry filtering. It is a test asset, but a single micro-benchmark is minor and maps to no specific testing element type such as a coverage target or test case sketch. It implements no cross-cutting concerns.

Exported config-parser method that opens a configuration file and parses it into options; it is invoked by the CLI parser. It is a notable internal unit of configuration loading, so it is modelled as an application function. It reads a file from disk, which counts as data persistence.

Unit test function verifying that the HTTP response builder writes a byte body. It is an individual test case realizing a test case sketch against the response builder, of minor significance and with no cross-cutting concerns implemented.

HTTP route handler (Miniflux UI) serving embedded JavaScript bundles by filename with caching headers and service-worker variable injection. It is a GET operation on a static-asset path, but a minor one. It does not render the UI itself, and it performs no persistence or authentication work.

A unit test function verifying that the locale printer falls back to the key when the language is missing. It is an individual test case in the testing layer, minor in significance, and implements no cross-cutting concerns.

Integration test function verifying the import feed entry endpoint is idempotent on re-import. It is a single test case that realizes a test case sketch in the testing layer. It is of minor significance. It calls the live API over HTTP through the client.

Method of the Shiori integration client that posts a bookmark to the external Shiori API. It is internal behaviour of an integration component that SendEntry invokes. It obtains a token through the separate authenticate method and only attaches it as a header, so it does not perform authentication itself. It is notable within the integration module but not a system boundary.

A single Go unit test that verifies the conversion of an entry ID to the Google Reader long-form item ID format. It is a concrete test case in the testing layer, but it is narrow and of minor architectural importance. It implements no cross-cutting concerns.

Trivial private helper returning the cookie path from the configured base path, defaulting to '/'. It is used by the session and preference cookie setters but does no authentication work itself. This is an implementation detail below the granularity of an architecture model.

Server-side page handler that renders the 'entry' HTML template for an unread entry. It loads the entry, pagination and nav counters from the store and toggles read status. It is best modelled as the routable unread-entry reading view of the web UI rather than as a JSON API operation.

This is the Slack integration client's core behaviour. It posts feed-entry notifications to an external Slack webhook over HTTP, so it is an application function realizing an outbound integration. It is notable within the integration module, but it is one of many notifier adapters. Its debug logging is incidental rather than observability work.

A trivial string-to-int64 parsing helper with a fallback value, used by the config line parser. It is an implementation detail below architectural granularity and implements none of the cross-cutting concerns.

An HTTP route handler for the OAuth2 account-unlink endpoint (provider path parameter) in the server-rendered UI. It checks the local-auth configuration, refuses to unlink when the user has no password, clears the provider profile ID through the store, and returns HTML redirects with flash messages and slog warnings. It is a named endpoint, so it is modelled as an api operation.

A table-driven unit test that checks EnclosureList.ContainsAudioOrVideo across MIME-type cases. It is a test asset, so it maps to a testing test case design. It is a minor, file-local unit with no cross-cutting concerns. The callee worker.Run is a call-graph artifact of t.Run.

A trivial fluent builder method that appends one SQL condition string to the EntryQueryBuilder. It does no I/O itself and is an implementation detail of the query builder, below the granularity of an architecture element. The enclosing builder or query layer would be modelled instead.

This is a trivial setter on the WebSession model. It records the OAuth2 state and PKCE verifier in session state and marks the session dirty. It supports authentication but is an accessor-level implementation detail, not an element in its own right. The session persistence itself happens elsewhere.

A single unit test function verifying parsing of the METRICS_COLLECTOR config option. It belongs in the testing layer as an individual test case, but it has minor significance because it is one of many config option tests. It does not itself implement metrics or any other concern.

A single Go unit test verifying that CharsetReader converts a file with an invalid XML prolog into valid UTF-8. It is an individual test case, so testcasesketch fits, but its significance is minor. Opening the testdata fixture is test scaffolding, not durable persistence.

This is the Discord integration client's behaviour: it posts webhook notifications for new feed entries to the external Discord API. It is an internal application function invoked by PushEntries and is a notable integration unit. The debug log line is incidental, not an observability concern in its own right.

A small internal step of the icon finder in Miniflux. It builds the /favicon.ico URL and delegates the download to downloadIcon, so the HTTP call happens elsewhere. The debug log line is incidental rather than telemetry. It is a minor fallback routine that only its file cares about.

Table-driven unit test for the private normalizeETag helper. It is a test asset, so it belongs to the testing layer as a test case. It verifies a small formatting detail, so its architectural significance is minor.

Individual Go unit test verifying the Atom parser trims trailing spaces in the feed self-link URL. It is a single test case exercising one input partition (a URL with whitespace), so it maps to a test case sketch of minor significance. It implements no cross-cutting concerns.

Fluent builder method that appends a SQL tag-filter condition to a pagination query builder. It is a small query-construction helper inside the storage layer and not an element in its own right. It does not execute I/O itself, and the parent builder or query would be the element a maintainer models.

A storage-layer DAO method that issues an INSERT into the feeds table and inserts the feed's entries inside per-entry transactions. It is a named write operation against the feeds collection that application code issues, so it fits the data-store AccessPattern type. It is notable but not central.

A small DOM helper that renders a transient toast feedback element. It is shared by several action handlers, so it works like a reusable UI widget, but it is a minor implementation-level unit. It renders user-facing UI and touches no other concern.

This is the private recursive tree-walking helper inside the HTML sanitizer. It filters nodes against the allow-list and writes escaped HTML into a buffer. It is an implementation detail of SanitizeHTML, the public sanitizer function that would be the modelled element, and is not an element in its own right.

This handler renders the 'offline' template as an HTML page, likely the PWA offline fallback screen. It is a small UI surface, a view, with no logic beyond rendering. It has minor significance, and its only concern is user interface.

HTTP route handler for the user creation endpoint (POST /users) in the REST API. It performs an inline admin-only access check, decodes and validates the request, then persists the user through the storage layer. That makes it an API operation with an authorization concern. Persistence is delegated to the store.

Trivial private template helper that checks whether a string parses as an email address. It is a formatting and validation utility below architectural granularity, has no cross-cutting responsibility, and its only caller is a unit test.

Trivial predicate on the Enclosure model. It checks the MIME type and URL suffix to decide whether the enclosure is an image. This is an implementation detail and accessor-level helper, not an architectural element. Only a unit test calls it.

A Go table-driven unit test exercising the private isDateMatchingPattern filter helper across partitions (future, before, after, between, max-age, invalid inputs). It is a test asset, so it belongs to the testing layer as a test case design. It has minor significance: a single unit test of an internal helper, with no cross-cutting concerns.

Private helper that parses a boolean string from config lines, falling back to a default when the value is empty. It is a trivial parsing utility below the granularity of an architectural element and implements no cross-cutting concern.

Storage-layer method issuing a named SQL read against the users table keyed by lowercased username. It is a repository query shape, an access pattern on the users collection. It is used by auth flows but does not itself verify identity. It is a notable but ordinary query among many in the storage package.

A small input-validation helper that checks offset/limit pagination parameters against bounds. It is called by one API handler and its test. It is too fine-grained to be an architectural element; at most it is an application-side check, not an engine-enforced or security validation rule.

A trivial fluent builder setter that adds an HTTP header to a RequestBuilder. It is an implementation detail of the fetcher component, not an architectural element. It makes no external call itself; it only records header state for the request that is built later.

A single Go unit test that verifies config file parsing. It writes a temporary file only as a test fixture. As a test case it belongs to the testing layer, but it is a minor, file-local verification unit. It implements no cross-cutting concern itself.

HTTP route handler implementing the Google Reader API /rename-tag endpoint. It parses form parameters, validates them and returns JSON or text responses, so it is an API operation contract. It updates the category in the store directly, which counts as persistence. The debug log line is incidental, not telemetry work.

Trivial serialization helper that copies Post fields into URL query values for the Pinboard API call. It is formatting/marshalling detail below architectural granularity. The integration work itself happens in CreateBookmark, not here.

A micro-benchmark function for the Accept-Encoding header parser. It is test scaffolding below the granularity of a test suite or coverage element, with no architectural role, so it is not modelled as an element.

Request-validation routine invoked by the API handler to check that an entries status/starred update request is well-formed. It is internal input-validation behaviour, a minor unit. It is not authorization logic and not a schema definition. The callee internal.ui.view.New appears to be a spurious graph edge.

Storage method issuing a single SQL read against the integrations table to check uniqueness of a Fever username. It is a minor query-layer access pattern in the data-store layer and reads durable storage. It does not itself verify credentials or decide permissions.

A table-driven unit test that verifies EnclosureList.ProxifyEnclosureURL across proxy modes and resource types. It is a test asset, so it belongs to the testing layer as a test case design. It has minor significance, mattering only to its own file, and implements no cross-cutting concerns itself.

An interface method declaration abstracting sql.Row/sql.Rows Scan, used so web session row-mapping helpers can accept either type. It is a trivial adapter signature with no behaviour, below the granularity of an architecture element. The caller list is inflated by name collision with database Scan calls.

Shared private helper used by three API entry handlers: runs a prepared storage query, rewrites media URLs through the proxy, and writes the JSON response. It is internal plumbing behind the operations rather than an endpoint itself. Persistence happens through the query builder it is given, so it implements no cross-cutting concern directly. Minor significance.

A single Go unit test verifying that parseRules correctly parses a rewrite-rule string. It is an individual test case within the testing layer, so testcasesketch is the closest fit. It is minor, of interest only to its file, and implements no cross-cutting concerns.

A trivial fluent builder setter that sets a boolean flag on RequestBuilder and returns the receiver. It contains no behaviour of its own and is an implementation detail of the fetcher component, so it is not an architectural element in its own right.

Unit test verifying that the XMLAttachment response helper sets the status, body, Content-Type and Content-Disposition headers. It is a single test case against a minor response utility, so its architectural significance is low. Callees such as storage.Get and telegrambot are graph-resolution noise for the Get and Result calls.

Private method of the Atom 1.0 adapter that maps parsed Atom entries to model entries, resolving URLs, content, title, dates, tags, hash and enclosures. It is a substantial internal transformation step within the feed parsing component, so it is an application function rather than a contract. Its debug logging is incidental, not telemetry.

A Go unit test that checks valid and invalid category sorting orders against a validator helper. It is a minor single-purpose test case, so it maps to a testcasesketch with low significance. It implements no cross-cutting concerns.

Private one-line string helper that checks for an http/https prefix and is used only by sibling URL utilities. It is an implementation detail with no architectural identity, so it gets no layer or element type.

A storage-layer method that issues a named bulk UPDATE against the entries table, joined with feeds and scoped by user, category and date. It is a write access pattern used by the API, Fever, Google Reader and UI handlers. Its debug logging is incidental, so observability is not marked.

Entry point of the RDF feed-format parser in Miniflux's reader. It decodes RDF XML and normalizes it into a model.Feed, and is dispatched by ParseFeed. This is internal parsing behaviour performed by the reader component, a notable unit within the feed-parsing module.

A trivial accessor on ResponseHandler that reads the Last-Modified HTTP header and suppresses it when Expires is 0. It is an implementation detail of the feed fetcher, not an architectural element. The listed storage callee is a mis-resolved Header.Get call, so the method performs no persistence.

A Go fuzz test for the feed parser. It seeds the fuzzer with Atom, RSS, RDF and JSON Feed samples and exercises ParseFeed with arbitrary input. This makes it a test asset that verifies the parser component, so it belongs in the testing layer as a test case design of moderate significance.

An HTTP route handler for the settings form submission (POST /settings). It validates the form, delegates the user update to the store, then re-renders the settings view or redirects. As a method-plus-path endpoint contract it is an API operation. It renders HTML directly; persistence is delegated to the store.

An HTTP route handler for the update-user endpoint (PUT /users/{userID}), so it maps to an API operation. It enforces authorization inline: a non-admin may edit only their own record and cannot grant admin. Persistence goes through store calls rather than being implemented here.

Verifies a web session secret against its stored hash with a constant-time comparison, so it is credential verification used when loading a session from a cookie. It is authentication logic but sits at method granularity, and no single security element type fits a session-secret check, so the element type is null.

A trivial setter on WebSession that assigns WebAuthn session data and marks the session dirty. It does no identity verification or persistence itself; the login flow in the callers does that work. As an accessor-level implementation detail it falls below the modelling granularity threshold.

Go unit test that verifies the HTTP client request builder: method, JSON content type, user agent, header and body, all checked against a local httptest server. As an individual test case it maps to a testcasesketch at low significance. It is test code, so it implements none of the cross-cutting concerns itself.

Front-end initializer that wires WebAuthn register, login and delete buttons to the WebAuthnHandler and enables them. It drives the UI controls for passkey authentication; the authentication protocol work itself sits in the handler. Best modelled as UX action wiring for the login and settings views. Notable but not core.

A small DOM scrolling helper that the keyboard-navigation functions call. It drives the UI viewport but is an implementation detail below the granularity of a UX element, so it gets no layer. The user_interface concern is still true because it manipulates the page directly.

Table-driven unit test that verifies the response builder's ETag and If-None-Match caching behaviour. It is a test asset, so it belongs in the testing layer as a test case design. It is a minor unit that matters only to its file. Callees such as storage.Get and worker.Run are graph noise, and the test implements none of the cross-cutting concerns itself.

Session ID and secret rotation upon authentication is an explicit session-fixation mitigation. It generates fresh credentials and hashes the secret, which makes it a security countermeasure. It is a small method, but a maintainer would name it when explaining web session security. Callers persist the result, so persistence is not this method's concern.

HTTP handler implementing the Fever API 'groups' operation for third-party clients: it reads categories and feeds through the store and returns the JSON groups response. It is one of several operations dispatched by serve, so it is moderately significant. It serves an external client protocol; persistence and logging happen in callees or are trivial.

A single unit test function verifying that FindClientIP honours the X-Real-Ip header from trusted proxies. It is one individual test case, which maps to a testcasesketch, but it has minor architectural significance. It implements no cross-cutting concern itself.

Storage-layer method that issues a DELETE against the users table, a single named write operation from repository code. It is best modelled as a data-store access pattern on the users collection. It is called by both the API and UI handlers, which makes it notable but not core.

A single Go unit test function that checks percent unescaping in the locale printer. It is test scaffolding below the granularity of a testing-layer element such as a coverage target or model, so it has negligible architectural significance and implements no cross-cutting concern.

A small mutex-guarded helper that appends a normalized proxy dial address to an in-memory trusted list. It is an implementation detail of the fetcher's request builder, not an element a maintainer would name in an architecture model.

A fluent builder method that only appends two SQL condition strings to the pagination query builder. It is a trivial query-construction helper below modelling granularity. It does not itself execute storage I/O, so no persistence concern is claimed.

Table-driven unit test verifying the String() formatting of readability candidate nodes. It is a test asset belonging to the testing layer, but it exercises a minor debug/formatting helper, so its architectural significance is low. It implements no cross-cutting concerns.

Cosmetic text-formatting utility that strips HTML tags from strings. Its docstring explicitly disclaims any security role. It is used by feed parsers as a helper, which places it below architectural granularity.

A storage-layer method that issues a single UPDATE against the entries table, clearing share_code scoped by user and entry. This is a named write access pattern issued from repository code. It is a minor unit, one of many similar Storage query methods.

Trivial private helper that joins accumulated SQL condition strings with AND. It is an implementation detail of the EntryQueryBuilder query layer and performs no storage I/O itself, so it is not an architecture element and not modelled on its own.

A single unit test case that verifies media proxy URL rewriting for video in http-only mode. It is one of many similar cases and fits the testcasesketch type. It has low significance and implements no cross-cutting concern itself.

Unit test function verifying that the Gotify client normalizes endpoint URL formats to /message. It is a single test case against a mock HTTP server, so it maps to a testcasesketch with low significance. It only exercises the integration client and does not itself perform external integration.

A fluent builder method on batchBuilder that only appends a SQL WHERE condition string to a slice. It does no I/O itself and is an implementation detail of the storage query builder, below the granularity of an architectural element. The batch query or access pattern as a whole would be the element.

Table-driven Go unit test that exercises the IsBlockedEntry filter function, covering block/allow rule precedence across several cases. It is test evidence, best modelled as a test case sketch, and has minor significance limited to its own module.

HTTP route handler in Miniflux's REST API serving GET /entries/{entryID}: it parses the path parameter, scopes the query to the requesting user and returns JSON. It is one method-path contract, so an api operation. Persistence is delegated to the storage query builder, so no concern is implemented directly.

A single Go unit test checking that NewCharsetReader converts an ISO-8859-1 XML fixture without a content type to UTF-8. It is one concrete test case realizing a coverage combination, so it maps to testcasesketch. It is minor, and opening a test fixture file is not durable persistence.

This is an HTTP handler on the Miniflux UI handler that serves the OPML import-from-URL form POST. It fetches a remote OPML file over HTTP and imports it into the store. It also renders the import page on error and logs via slog. As a route handler bound to a method and path, it is modelled as an API operation.

This is a Matrix client method that authenticates against an external homeserver by POSTing credentials and receiving an access token. It is internal integration behaviour of the Matrix bot client component, so it is modelled as an application function. It performs authentication and external HTTP integration.

A request-context accessor that returns the logged-in user's ID, read from a context value or from the web session. It has very high fan-in, but it is a helper rather than a named architectural element. It works with authenticated identity via the session, though the actual verification happens in middleware elsewhere.

A single unit test verifying that the JSONNotFound helper returns a 404 status, the expected error body and the JSON content type. It is a minor individual test case, modelled at most as a test case sketch of low significance, and it implements no cross-cutting concern itself.

This method wires DOM touch-event listeners for the TouchHandler gesture component in Miniflux's web UI. It is a UI interaction detail inside a client-side component, not an element on its own. Modelling would happen at the TouchHandler level, so no element type fits and significance is low.

This is an individual Go unit test. It checks that the fetcher's RequestBuilder routes requests through an environment-configured proxy even when private networks are disallowed. It maps to one test case in the testing layer and has low significance. It uses a local httptest server, so it implements no cross-cutting concern itself.

Shaarli integration client method that POSTs a bookmark to the external Shaarli API at /api/v1/links. It is the core behaviour of the integration adapter, invoked by SendEntry. It attaches a bearer token generated elsewhere but does not verify identity itself, so authentication is false. External integration is true.

Small input-validation routine (Miniflux-style) checking that the title and content of an entry update request are non-empty. It is called by the API handler. This is internal application behaviour rather than security access logic or a schema definition, and its architectural significance is minor.

Internal processor function (Miniflux reader) that calls the external Bilibili HTTP API to fetch a video's duration and compute the watch time in minutes. It is an application function performing an integration with a third-party API. Its slog warning is incidental logging, not a telemetry element.

Private method of the webhook Client that POSTs HMAC-signed JSON payloads to an external webhook URL. It is the outbound integration mechanism, but as an unexported helper behind the public Send*WebhookEvent functions it is a minor internal unit. It performs external HTTP integration; signing is message integrity, not authentication of a caller.

A unit test function that verifies the getContextBoolValue helper returns false for a non-bool context value. As a single test case it maps to a testing-layer test case sketch. It has minor significance and implements no cross-cutting concern itself.

Upsert of a single key into the acme_cache table. It implements the autocert Cache interface for certificate storage, and the query is issued from application code. This makes it a write access pattern on that collection, and it does real database persistence. It is a small method within the certificate cache component, so significance is low.

HTTP route handler for listing users (GET /users) in the API package; it is one method-path operation contract. It performs an inline admin check (authorization) and reads users via the store, but persistence is delegated to the store, so data_persistence is false.

An individual unit test function verifying that the RSS parser maps an iTunes summary to the entry content. As a single test case it best fits testcasesketch in the testing layer, with low significance because it is one of many parser tests.

A single Go unit test checking that parseImageDataURL rejects a non-image MIME type. It is an individual test case that exercises a validation-error outcome. It is a minor, file-local unit with no cross-cutting concerns.

Storage-layer method issuing a single UPDATE against the integrations table for one user's settings, which makes it a named write access pattern on a collection. It persists data directly. It is notable but a single repository operation, not a central component.

An HTTP route handler in Miniflux's UI package that toggles an entry's starred state and returns JSON. It is one method-path endpoint, so it is modelled as an API operation. Persistence is delegated to the store, so the handler does not implement the data_persistence concern itself. Its significance is moderate.

A unit test function verifying that the RequestBuilder preserves a custom Accept header. It is an individual test case using an httptest server stub, a minor test unit and not a production integration point.

HTTP route handler for the REST API's update-feed endpoint (PUT /feeds/{feedID}). It decodes the request, validates it, scopes the lookup to the user, persists the change via the store and returns JSON responses. It is one method-path contract, so it is an api operation. The concerns are delegated to the store and request helpers, so none are flagged.

Generic private helper that appends mapped variadic values into a sorted slice by delegating to appendSortedSeq. It is a trivial utility used by the tag-extraction functions in the RSS adapter, an implementation detail rather than an architectural element.

This API middleware verifies the X-Auth-Token API key, resolves the user and sets the authenticated context. It is the API key authentication mechanism, so it belongs in the security layer. It logs authentication outcomes via slog. Storage writes go through store calls, so it does not persist data itself.

A shared factory for the outbound HTTP client, used by many third-party integrations. It optionally installs a connect-time dialer that refuses private or loopback IPs as SSRF protection. It works as a cross-cutting outbound connectivity function rather than an API contract. The SSRF guard could also be modelled as a security countermeasure.

Exported entry filtering decision used by the feed processor: it applies block, allow, blocklist and keeplist rules to decide whether an entry is dropped. This is internal application behaviour (content filtering, not access control). It is a notable unit a maintainer would name when explaining feed processing.

Internal sub-handler dispatched by streamItemIDsHandler for the Google Reader starred stream. It builds a storage query for starred entries, applies time and paging filters, and writes the JSON item-ID response. It is not a route on its own, so it is modelled as behaviour behind the stream IDs API operation. Query execution happens in a callee.

HTTP route handler in the web UI that removes an API key for the current user. It reads the keyID route parameter, delegates deletion to the storage layer, and redirects to the keys page. It is one method-path endpoint, so it is modelled as an api operation of modest significance. Persistence is delegated to the store.

Integration test function verifying that regular users are denied access to the get-user-by-username endpoint. It is a single test case realizing an authorization-error outcome for an API operation, so it maps to a testcasesketch. It calls the external API over HTTP but does not itself implement auth checks.

A trivial fluent setter on the HTTP response Builder that flips a compression flag. It is an implementation detail of the builder, below the granularity of an architectural element, and it implements no cross-cutting concern itself.

A fluent builder setter on EntryQueryBuilder that only sets a flag. It is a query-option toggle, not an architectural element itself. The query builder as a whole could be modelled as a data-store access pattern, but this method sits below that granularity and performs no storage I/O directly.
Trivial private CLI helper that formats an error and delegates to printErrorAndExit. It is an implementation detail with no architectural identity. It writes no output itself, so no concern applies.

Trivial one-line accessor exposing the sql.DB connection pool statistics to a metrics gatherer. It does no telemetry work itself and does no storage I/O beyond reading in-memory pool counters. It is an implementation detail of the Storage component, not an element in its own right.

Wraps the Prometheus promhttp handler to expose the process's metrics to an external scraper. In OpenTelemetry terms this is a pull-based metric exporter. It delegates the access decision to isAllowedToAccessMetricsEndpoint and logs denied attempts. As the telemetry export boundary of the service, it is architecturally significant.

A Go unit test verifying that the Gotify client's SendMessage posts the correct token, headers and body to a mock HTTP server. It is an individual test case, modelled as a test case sketch in the testing layer, with low architectural significance. It only exercises the integration client against a local mock, so no concern is implemented by the test itself.

Storage-layer repository method that issues a named read query (per-user read and unread feed counters) against the feeds and entries tables via the query builder. It models a specific read access pattern called by the API handler, so it is a notable but not core unit.

An individual integration test case that exercises the DELETE category API operation through the Miniflux client as a regular user. It maps to a single test case sketch tied to one endpoint. HTTP calls and credentials are handled by the client library, not implemented by the test itself.

A table-driven unit test for the IsAbsoluteURL helper in the urllib package. It is a test asset, modelled at most as a test case sketch against a utility function. It sits in the testing layer but has low architectural significance and implements no cross-cutting concerns.

Server-rendered page handler for the search-result entry screen. It loads the entry for the current user, marks it read, computes previous/next navigation and renders the 'entry' template. It is best modelled as a UX view (a page), not a JSON API operation. It writes entry status to the store.

A single Go unit test verifying that the HTML sanitizer strips an unknown nested tag while keeping valid inner tags. As an individual test case it maps to a testcasesketch, but it is minor, one of many sanitizer tests in its file.

A single unit test function that verifies the YouTube link rewrite rule of the content rewriter. As a test case, it maps to a testcasesketch in the testing layer. It is a minor individual case among many similar rewrite tests, so its significance is low.

Trivial setter on a private parsing-result struct in the srcset sanitizer. It only assigns two fields and is called by a single parser function, so it is an implementation detail below the granularity of any architecture element.

A unit test function that checks the HTTP response builder sets a custom header. It is a single test case realizing a test case sketch for the response builder. Its significance is minor, and it implements no cross-cutting concern. The callee resolutions to storage and telegrambot are spurious name matches.

Small private helper of subscriptionFinder that parses an already-fetched HTML document for a canonical link tag and resolves it to an absolute URL. It performs no I/O itself and is an implementation detail of FindSubscriptions, below the granularity of an architectural element.

Server-side HTTP form-submission handler for saving a user's third-party integration settings (Fever, Google Reader, webhook, Linktaco). It validates input, derives credentials (Fever token, hashed Google Reader password, webhook secret), delegates persistence to the store, and drives the web UI via flash messages and redirects. It is one route operation, so significance is moderate.

Integration test function exercising the GET feed API endpoint via the HTTP client against a running server; it is a single test case realizing a test case sketch for the feed retrieval operation. Minor significance as one of many endpoint tests; it calls an external server over HTTP.

This is a server-side HTML page handler in Miniflux's UI package. It renders the 'tag_entries' template listing all entries for a tag, with pagination, so it is best modelled as a UX view (a routable page). Storage access goes through the store, which the handler only calls, so data persistence is not its own concern.

HTTP handler for the authentication-settings form POST: it verifies the current password, updates the username and password, revokes other sessions and re-authenticates the current one. It is modelled as an endpoint operation. It also persists through the store, logs failed attempts and renders HTML responses.

An individual unit test function verifying that the RSS parser tolerates invalid enclosure length values. It is a single test case realizing a sketch in the testing layer, with minor significance and no cross-cutting concerns implemented itself.

A single unit test function that checks the RSS parser's handling of content:encoded. It maps to a test case sketch in the testing layer and has low significance as one of many parser tests. It implements no cross-cutting concern itself.

Client-side WebAuthn passkey registration flow: fetches creation options, invokes the browser credentials API, posts the attestation to the server and redirects. It implements credential enrollment, so it belongs to the security layer. No type fits a client ceremony exactly; authenticationconfig is the closest. It drives the UI through error messages and the redirect, and calls the server endpoints.

An HTTP route handler in Miniflux's server-rendered UI that removes a feed from a category. It is bound to one method and path, so it is modelled as an API operation. It drives the UI through a redirect. Persistence is delegated to the store, and the ownership check runs in the store via UserID.

An integration test function that exercises the update-user API endpoint over HTTP via the Miniflux client, checking that external font hosts are trimmed. It is one concrete test case realizing a coverage requirement, so it maps to a testcasesketch with minor significance.

Shared internal helper of the web UI handler that rate-limits forced refreshes, builds feed refresh jobs from the store and pushes them to the worker pool. It is not itself a route handler (it is called by two page handlers), so it is modelled as an application function. It logs via slog and sets UI flash messages.

Trivial constructor that only stores the base URL and credentials in a struct, with no logic of its own. The Shiori client type would be the modelled integration component; this factory is boilerplate below model granularity and performs no integration or authentication work itself.

A Go unit test function that verifies resizeIcon downsizes a 33x33 PNG to 32x32. It is a single test case for an internal helper and maps to a testcasesketch. It has low architectural significance and implements no cross-cutting concerns.

HTTP route handler (Miniflux media proxy endpoint) taking encodedDigest/encodedURL path params. It verifies an HMAC signature to authorize proxying, fetches the remote media over HTTP, blocks private-network targets, emits structured logs, and streams the response with caching headers. It is an architecturally significant integration endpoint.

An individual unit test function that verifies the JSON feed parser prefers the item url over external_url. It maps to a single test case realizing one coverage scenario of the parser. Its significance is minor because it is one of many parser tests.

Internal configuration-parser method that validates one key/value pair and converts it to a typed option. It is part of the config component's parsing behaviour but is an internal step called only by parseLines. Secret-file reading is delegated to a callee, and the deprecation warning is incidental logging rather than telemetry.

Core transformation in the JSON Feed reader adapter: it maps a parsed JSON Feed document onto the internal model.Feed and its entries, resolving URLs, normalizing language, choosing fallbacks and parsing dates. It is internal behaviour of the reader component, invoked by Parse. The debug logging is incidental and does not make the method an observability element.

A storage-layer method that issues one ad hoc UPDATE against the categories table, keyed by id and user_id. This is a named write access pattern issued from repository code rather than logic stored in the engine. It is a notable but routine unit used by the API, Google Reader and UI handlers.

Go unit test exercising boundary values for validateEntriesPerPage (valid 1 and max; invalid 0, -1, max+1). A small test case in the testing layer that realizes a boundary-value test design. It has minor significance and implements no cross-cutting concerns.

Constructor for the TLS certificate loader. It loads the key pair from disk and logs the event. This is a factory/helper below modelling granularity; the certificateLoader type or the TLS configuration would be the element instead. It reads files and emits a log line.

A single Go unit test that checks a boundary partition (limit=0 falls back to the default of 10000) for the entry-IDs query parameter parsing. It is a minor test-case-level element that verifies the API parameter handling. It implements no cross-cutting concern itself.

Storage method issuing a single SQL read against the api_keys table, keyed by user_id and description, used to enforce uniqueness during validation. It is a data-store access pattern, though a minor one. It reads the database but does not itself verify credentials or perform authentication.

A single unit test function verifying that the RSS parser handles encoded angle brackets in descriptions. It is a test case in the testing layer, one of many parser tests, so it carries minor significance. It implements none of the cross-cutting concerns.

Storage-layer method issuing a single keyed SELECT against the webauthn_credentials table by handle. It is a named read access pattern used by login and credential management flows. It reads credential data but performs no identity verification itself, so authentication is not set.

A trivial setter on the Feed model that assigns a Category stub with the given ID. It is an accessor-level implementation detail of the Feed entity, not an architectural element in its own right, despite its many callers. It implements none of the cross-cutting concerns.

An HTTP route handler for the REST API (Miniflux) that implements DELETE /categories/{categoryID}. It is a single method-path API operation. It scopes the category to the current user ID and delegates persistence to the store, so it does not perform storage or authentication itself.

A single Go unit test function. It verifies that the HTTP response builder applies gzip compression when the client accepts it and the body exceeds the threshold. As an individual test case it maps to a testcasesketch with low significance. Its callees to storage and the UI view are graph resolution noise; it implements no cross-cutting concern.

A table-driven Go unit test for the private isSameSite helper in the fetcher's request builder. It is a test asset, so it maps to a testcasesketch in the testing layer. It covers only a small internal helper, which gives it low architectural significance.

A table-driven unit test of the private isCJK helper in the reading-time module. It is a test asset, so it belongs in the testing layer, best typed as a test case sketch with several input selections. It has low significance because it verifies a minor internal helper. The worker.Run callee is a resolution artifact of t.Run.

Query-builder method in Miniflux's storage layer that issues an ad hoc SQL SELECT joining feeds, categories, icons and users, then scans rows into model.Feeds. It is a read access pattern against the feeds collection, issued from application code. It is notable within the storage module but is not a standalone service.

HTTP route handler in Miniflux UI handler that exports the user's feeds as an OPML attachment. It is a method-path endpoint contract, so it is modelled as an api operation.
