The persistence and OPML generation are delegated to the opml handler and the store, so the handler implements no cross-cutting concern itself.

Calls an external RSS-Bridge service over HTTP (findfeed action) to discover feeds for a website and normalizes the bridge URLs it returns. It is the core integration function of the rssbridge client and is used by subscription discovery. Debug logging is incidental, and passing a token as a query parameter is not identity verification by this function.

A single Go unit test checking that the version string contains digits and converts to a positive integer, a client-compatibility expectation. It is a narrow test case of minor significance. Callee names are graph noise from strings.Builder methods, not real persistence or config access.

Trivial accessor on LocalizedError that wraps its string message in a Go error. Despite many callers, it is a conversion helper: an implementation detail below architectural granularity, with no cross-cutting concern.

A single Go unit test checking that the JSON Feed parser de-duplicates and sorts item authors. It is a test case in the testing layer, best typed as a testcasesketch. It is a minor unit relevant only to its own file. It implements no cross-cutting concerns.

Trivial accessor on WebAuthnUser that satisfies the webauthn library's User interface by mapping stored credentials into a slice. It sits in the WebAuthn authentication flow but only reshapes data, so it is an implementation detail rather than a modelled element, and it does not itself verify identity.

A server-rendered page handler for the unread-in-category entry screen. It loads the entry, updates its read status, computes previous/next navigation and renders the 'entry' HTML template. It is best modelled as the UX view it delivers, not as a JSON API operation. It reads and writes storage through the store.

A trivial String() accessor on LocalizedError that formats the error message with the en_US printer. It is a formatting helper and an implementation detail, not an architectural element in its own right.

A single Go unit test checking that the RSS parser prefers the feedburner:origLink element when it sets the entry URL. It is one test case realizing a coverage requirement of the RSS parser target, so it is a test case sketch of minor significance. It implements no cross-cutting concerns.

An internal image-processing routine in the icon finder: it minifies SVG icons, rejects oversized images and scales raster icons down to 32x32 PNG. It is a private step called by downloadIcon. The logging it does is incidental diagnostics, not telemetry design. Modelled as a minor application function.

A storage-layer method that runs a transactional SQL count, update and delete against the categories and feeds tables. It is a named write operation issued from repository code, so it is a data-store access pattern of moderate significance, used by the Google Reader tag-disable handler.

Go unit test checking edge cases of the private isDateMatchingPattern filter helper (boundary between-dates and max-age in hours). It is an individual test case realizing a test design, so it maps to a testing testcasesketch, but it has minor significance and implements no cross-cutting concerns.

A trivial fluent builder method that only appends a SQL condition and argument to the query builder's in-memory state. It executes no query and touches no storage itself. As an implementation detail of the EntryQueryBuilder data-store access layer, it is not an architectural element on its own.

A table-driven unit test for a private helper (hasFormattingDirective) in the locale printer. It is a test case realizing a small test design, so it belongs to testing as a test case sketch, but it has minimal architectural significance and touches no cross-cutting concern.

A trivial one-line accessor on the Atom category collection that returns sorted, deduplicated names by delegating to makeSorted. It is a feed-parsing implementation detail below the granularity of any architectural element, with no cross-cutting concerns.

A trivial constructor that parses username and password form values from an HTTP request into an authForm struct. It does not verify credentials itself; checkLogin does that. As a parsing helper below modelling granularity, it is not an architectural element on its own.

A server-side HTML page handler that renders the 'entry' template for an entry within a category, with prev/next navigation and unread counts. It is a user-facing screen (view), not a JSON API contract. Storage and marking entries as read are delegated to the store, so persistence is only called, not implemented here.
